questions.q: What are the two stages of the Create Accounting process?
options: Credit check, then approval
Pick, then pack
Create final accounting in Subledger Accounting, then transfer to General Ledger and post
Request, then authorization
questions.explain: Create Accounting finalizes subledger events, then transfers and posts them into the General Ledger.

questions.q: What is the difference between draft and final accounting?
options: Draft is a preview that cannot post; only final accounting is eligible to transfer to GL
There is no real difference
Draft accounting is always more accurate than final
Final accounting only applies to cash receipts
questions.explain: Draft accounting is a non-postable preview; final accounting is the only version eligible to transfer and post.

questions.q: Why can a transaction's accounting be complete in Receivables before it's visible in the General Ledger?
options: Because Receivables and GL use entirely separate charts of accounts
Because Receivables transactions never actually post
Because GL only updates once per year
Because transfer and posting to GL can be batched at defined intervals rather than happening immediately
questions.explain: Transfer and posting can run on a schedule separate from when the subledger accounting itself was finalized.

questions.q: Once Create Accounting completes for SO-48217's entries, where do they ultimately land?
options: Nowhere — they remain invisible forever
The receivable, revenue, and cash accounts defined in the chart of accounts, visible in the period's GL balances
Only in a private Order Management log
Only in the customer's own accounting system
questions.explain: Posted entries become part of the GL's period balances in the relevant receivable, revenue, and cash accounts.

questions.q: What does it mean that an entry is "tagged back to its originating transaction" through Subledger Accounting?
options: Nothing — SLA entries are anonymous and untraceable
It means the entry can never be reviewed again
The finalized subledger journal retains a link back to the specific invoice, credit memo, or receipt that generated it
It means the entry bypasses the chart of accounts
questions.explain: SLA preserves a traceable link between a finalized journal entry and the originating business transaction.
